The data frame the sentence reads

Source: R/sentence.R
sentence_data.Rd

The data tokens of a sentence ({n}, {label(col)}, {col}, {filters}) and the column labels in the menu of a word read a data frame. The script block calls this generic on its first input to get one, so a package whose blocks hand on something else can say what the sentence sees.

Usage

sentence_data(x, script = NULL, ...)

# Default S3 method
sentence_data(x, script = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

The block's first input.

script

The block's script, one string. A method can read it to answer for the tables the script names.

...

Not used by the default method.

Value

A data frame, or NULL when the sentence has nothing to read.

Details

The default method returns a data frame as it is. A dm gives one data frame with the columns of all its tables side by side and no rows, with the column labels kept. Where two tables have a column of the same name, the first table's is used. {label(col)} then works for a column of any table, and {n} is 0. Anything else gives NULL: the data tokens are empty then, and a clause in [ ... ] that holds one leaves.

A method returns a data frame or NULL. A character vector in the attribute blockr_filters of that data frame is the filter trail that {filters} prints and that result_titles() returns as filters.

Examples

sentence_data(datasets::iris[1:3, ])
#>   Sepal.Length Sepal.Width Petal.Length Petal.Width Species
#> 1          5.1         3.5          1.4         0.2  setosa
#> 2          4.9         3.0          1.4         0.2  setosa
#> 3          4.7         3.2          1.3         0.2  setosa
sentence_data("not a data frame")
#> NULL

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# A package whose blocks hand on a dm with a filter trail
sentence_data.dm <- function(x, script = NULL, ...) {
  out <- NextMethod()
  attr(out, "blockr_filters") <- my_filter_trail(x)
  out
}
} # }
